name: Walchsee
kurzbeschreibung: Vacation spot at Walchsee with poolside vibes in summer and the Zahmer Kaiser ski area in winter.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Walchsee is situated at an elevation of approximately 660 metres above sea level in Tyrol's Kaiserwinkl region within the Kufstein district, nestled between the Zahmer Kaiser range and the Chiemgau Alps along the Bavarian frontier. With roughly 2,200 inhabitants, the village encompasses the historic centre as well as picturesque hamlets including Durchholzen, Schwaigs, and Oed. The natural crown jewel of the community is Lake Walchsee itself, a natural freshwater lake spanning nearly 100 hectares that reaches summer water temperatures of up to 24 degrees Celsius, ranking among the warmest bathing lakes in Tyrol. Beyond swimming lidos and modern water-sports facilities, Walchsee hosts the Schwemm, North Tyrol's largest contiguous raised bog. The community combines summer lakeside recreation, pristine conservation areas, and diverse alpine hiking without mass tourism.

Geschichte

The name Walchsee traces back to the 'Walchen', the Germanic designation for the Romanised Celtic inhabitants who persisted in this sheltered basin following the fall of the Western Roman Empire. The earliest written documentation appears in 1073 in records of the Bavarian monastery of Rott under the Latin entry 'vicus Romanicus' (Romans' village). In 1151 Pope Eugene III confirmed monastic holdings at Walchsee and Durchholzen. For centuries the Kaiserwinkl belonged to the domain of Bavarian dukes until Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I captured Kufstein during the Landshut War of Succession in 1504, permanently annexing the territory to Habsburg Tyrol. The parish church dedicated to Saint John the Baptist was documented in 1399 as a subsidiary of Ebbs, undergoing Baroque remodelling in 1729 and subsequent enlargement in the 18th century, preserving historic altarpieces and ceiling frescoes.

Anreise

Walchsee benefits from effortless travel connections from both Austria and Germany. Motorists arriving from the north via Munich travel along motorways A8 and A93 to the Oberaudorf or Kiefersfelden exits, continuing toll-free via Niederndorf on the B172 Walchsee federal road straight into the village. Approaching from Innsbruck or Salzburg, drivers take the Inntal Autobahn A12 exiting at Kufstein and continue via Ebbs and Niederndorf. Rail passengers arrive at the major cross-border railway junction in Kufstein, served by frequent ICE, Railjet, and EuroCity trains. From the station forecourt, the regional Kaiserwinkl bus (line 4030) runs regular services directly to Walchsee village centre, the lake promenade, and Durchholzen.

Tipps

A summer excursion to Lake Walchsee offers outstanding bathing at the public lakeside lidos, stand-up paddleboarding, electric boat hire, and the floating Wibit aqua park featuring inflatable obstacles, trampolines, and water slides. Nature lovers must visit the Schwemm nature reserve in the hamlet of Schwaigs: North Tyrol's largest contiguous bog complex is protected under Natura 2000 and can be admired from a 16-metre-high barrier-free observation tower equipped with educational display boards. In Durchholzen, the Zahmer Kaiser leisure arena features a chairlift, twin summer toboggan runs, and a forest playground. Mountain hikers enjoy ascents up the Wandberg and Heuberg, rewarding treks with mountain cheese tastings at the Burgeralm and panoramic views across the lake and the Kaisergebirge.
